**(a) Adopted readings and framework data.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable
and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4) and the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7), together with the
Boltzmann-constant and temperature conventions of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Declare one of the
following model readings of the same **adopted Gibbs assignment**:

(i) a fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]], on its sector space,
with Gibbs generator $G:=H_N^\sigma$; or

(ii) a separately declared number-variable mode model, such as a one-mode
bosonic Fock space, a fermionic occupation space, or a declared countable
independent-mode space, with its declared assigned observables and energy
operator $H$. The model declares a self-adjoint Gibbs generator $G$ on that
space: either $G=H$, or a separately supplied self-adjoint realization of the
effective generator $G=H-\mu\mathcal N$, where $\mathcal N$ is the declared
particle-number operator and $\mu\in\mathbb R$ is an assigned chemical
potential in joules. The subtraction is an operator with its supplied domain,
not an assertion that a formal unbounded difference is self-adjoint.

In either reading assume $G$ is bounded below and give its spectral PVM
$E_G$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Let $T>0$ be an assigned temperature in
kelvin and let $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$ with the assigned
Boltzmann constant $k_B$. The Gibbs assignment to either model, and the
chemical-potential identification in (ii), are additional physical
preparation assumptions made here; they are not derived from P1-P4 or from
the fixed-$N$ construction. In (ii) no restriction on the assigned real
$\mu$ is imposed beyond the declared generator and trace existence
conditions; the mode-specific convergence conditions are proved separately.
For reading (ii), $G$ specifies the Gibbs weights. If the assigned autonomous
dynamics is generated by $H$, stationarity of the Gibbs density requires its
separate dynamical or commutation hypotheses; this assignment does not
identify $H-\mu\mathcal N$ with the physical evolution generator.
The physical Helmholtz free-energy vocabulary of the entropy definition
continues to apply only to its stated nonzero finite-sector class and is not
extended to every effective generator by this postulate.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral calculus.

**(b) Existence hypothesis and the Gibbs preparation.** The model assumes
that the **partition trace is strictly positive and finite**:
$$0<Z:=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta G}<\infty,$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}B:=\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\langle Bf,f\rangle$ for a
bounded positive $B$ and an orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$, with value allowed
to be $+\infty$. Such a basis exists under the declared AC by the maximal
orthonormal-family argument using [[thm-zorn]] and the zero-complement
criterion of [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]].
This trace is basis independent: for $C:=B^{1/2}$ of
[[thm-positive-square-root]], the defining sum is
$\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\|Cf\|^2$, whose invariance is
[[thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent]]. When the sum is finite,
$C$ is Hilbert-Schmidt ([[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]), so $B=C^2$ is
trace class by [[thm-trace-class-iff-product-of-two-hilbert-schmidt-operators]],
and its ordinary trace is this same diagonal sum by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Apply this to the bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta G}$, since the
declared Gibbs generator $G$ is bounded below. The model
adopts as the **canonical** or **Gibbs preparation** of the declared model
at temperature $T$ the density operator
$$\rho_\beta:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta G}.$$
If the sector is zero-dimensional, its partition trace is $Z=0$, no
trace-one density exists, and no canonical density or equilibrium free
energy is assigned. On a nonzero finite-dimensional model space, $Z$ is a
positive finite sum $\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ over the eigenvalues of $G$; no energy
sign restriction is needed. There $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]], and the
strict positivity and finiteness hypothesis is automatic. In reading (i),
$Z=Z_N$ and this is precisely the finite-sector Gibbs assignment.

Outside the finite-dimensional class the existence hypothesis is a genuine
restriction. For a declared non-interacting fixed-$N$ model with a supplied
countably infinite orthonormal eigenmode basis and real mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ bounded below, the complete construction and trace criterion
of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-fixed-n-countable-mode-partition-criterion]] give
$Z_N=h_N(q)$ for bosonic statistics or $Z_N=e_N(q)$ for fermionic statistics,
where $q_j=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}$ and $h_N,e_N$ are the corresponding
nonnegative occupation-series sums. For every fixed $N\ge1$, either trace is
finite exactly when $\sum_jq_j<\infty$. This is a trace on the fixed-$N$
sector and permits negative mode energies.

For the separately declared full bosonic Fock models of reading (ii),
the single-mode calculation of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] and the product
criterion of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]]
provide the separate mathematical full-Fock traces, with their original
positive mode-energy hypotheses: they sum over every particle number,
including the vacuum, giving $(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$ for one mode
and $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j})^{-1}$ for countably many modes.
Their physical Gibbs reading is the additional assignment of (a)(ii), not a
consequence of a mathematical trace formula. Those full-Fock traces are not
substituted for the fixed-$N$ partition trace of reading (i).

**(c) The equilibrium assumption and thermal means.** The model **assumes**
that, for a declared sample of the species at the assigned temperature $T$
and in the absence of further preparation information, the preparation
description of the sample is $\rho_\beta$ in the sense of P1. For an assigned
sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ with spectral PVM $E_A$, define its outcome law
$\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta E_A(B))$ as in
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).
If and only if the absolute first moment is finite,
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|a|\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a)<\infty,$$
the model defines the **thermal mean** at temperature $T$ by
$$\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\int_{\mathbb R}a\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a),$$
read in the assigned unit $u_A$. For bounded $A$ this equals
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$. For
unbounded $A$, if the mean exists and the literal product $A\rho_\beta$ is
defined on the whole Hilbert space and is trace class, the mean also equals
$\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$ and
$\operatorname{tr}(\overline{\rho_\beta A})$; these conditional product
identities are proved by the density eigenexpansion in
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-spectral-mean-and-defined-trace-product]]. First-moment
existence alone imposes no such product or operator-square-domain condition.
When the absolute first moment is infinite the model asserts no finite
thermal mean. The identification of the parameter $T$ with the thermodynamic temperature of a
sample, and of $\beta$ with its inverse temperature, is part of this
assumption; the stated conservation and equilibrium properties of
$\rho_\beta$ under the flow of P4, and the extremal property of $\rho_\beta$
among preparations, are separate conditional results of this pair.

**(d) Motivation and status.** The assumption is motivated, but not
established, by the maximum-entropy reasoning of the cited sources: among
preparations with a prescribed mean energy, the Gibbs weights maximize the
entropy functional, and the finite-dimensional comparison theorem makes
$\rho_\beta$ the minimizer of the corresponding functional built from $G$.
Its physical Helmholtz free-energy reading applies in the stated finite
fixed-sector class; an effective-generator interpretation in a different
mode model is a separate declared reading. That reasoning is
an argument inside mathematical statistics and thermodynamics; it does not
derive the physical assumption that a sample is described by $\rho_\beta$.
The postulate is an **adopted** statistical-mechanical assumption of the
model, in the sense of the content model's distinction between adopted
assumptions and derived consequences.

**(e) Scope.** The postulate asserts nothing about how a sample reaches the
Gibbs preparation; in particular it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration
time, no ergodicity, no master-equation or Markov approximation, no
thermodynamic limit, no pressure, volume or phase-transition structure, and
no measured temperature or expectation. The requirement $0<Z<\infty$ is part
of the assumption; the model does not define a canonical preparation when
$Z=0$ or the partition trace diverges. Any comparison with a laboratory sample requires the
declared preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7, and
agreement of a thermal prediction with data is evidence about the combined
model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework or of this
postulate.
premise_quotes: [F1] [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]: for a declared $G=H$ model with self-adjoint semibounded generator and $0<\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}<\infty$, the adopted preparation is $\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$; the postulate explicitly assumes AC and Countable Choice and does not assert equilibration.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice and the canonical Gibbs-preparation assumption [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]. Restrict to its $G=H$ branch: the declared energy operator $H$ is self-adjoint, bounded below, and measured in joules; $T>0$ is in kelvins, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ is in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and $K_\beta=e^{-\beta H}$ has $0<Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}K_\beta<\infty$. Suppose also that on an open interval $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ containing $\beta$, every compact $C\subset J_\beta$ admits a summable family $a_j\ge0$ with $(1+|E_j|^2)e^{-\gamma E_j}\le a_j$ for all energy eigenvalues $E_j$ and $\gamma\in C$. Let $(u_j)$ be the finite or countable complete orthonormal eigenfamily supplied by [[thm-tdmath-general-trace-gibbs-model]], repeated according to multiplicity, with $Hu_j=E_ju_j$, and put $\lambda_j=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_\beta$. The supplied trace identity gives $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, and these $\lambda_j$ are the eigenvalues of $\rho_\beta$. Define the spectral mean $\bar E_\beta:=\sum_j\lambda_jE_j$, the variance $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(H):=\sum_j\lambda_j(E_j-\bar E_\beta)^2$, the dimensionless entropy $s_\beta:=-\sum_j\lambda_j\log\lambda_j$, and the physical von Neumann entropy $S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta):=k_{\mathrm B}s_\beta$. These are spectral-sum definitions for this commuting Gibbs density; no operator trace of an unbounded product is used. The supplied moment envelope makes these sums finite. Then
$$-\partial_\beta\log Z_\beta=\bar E_\beta,\qquad \partial_\beta^2\log Z_\beta=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(H),\qquad S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta)=k_{\mathrm B}\bigl(\log Z_\beta+\beta\bar E_\beta\bigr).$$
Thus $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z_\beta=\bar E_\beta-T S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta)$. This statement does not extend the Helmholtz interpretation to an effective generator $H-\mu\mathcal N$.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statement of isolated autonomous dynamics. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), which are the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral and group suppliers.

**(i) Energy operator.** An **isolated autonomous system** of the sector has a declared **energy operator** $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ that is self-adjoint ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) and a declared energy unit in which its spectral coordinate is read. The energy operator is part of the model specification of the system; for a massive particle it is fixed by the kinematics postulate P5, and singular or unbounded model Hamiltonians require their own self-adjointness statements.

**(ii) Evolution.** The time evolution of the model is the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),\qquad U(t+s)=U(t)U(s),\quad U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1},$$
defined by the spectral calculus of the self-adjoint generator ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]], [[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The energy unit enters the argument of the exponential so that $H_{\mathrm{op}}t/\hbar$ acts in the dimensionless spectral variable.

**(iii) State evolution.** A vector state evolves continuously, $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the Schroedinger equation
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(t)$$
holds in the norm-differentiable sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, where the derivative is the norm limit of the difference quotients; for other vectors the equation is not asserted, although the evolution remains continuous. A density-operator preparation evolves as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$, which is a density operator for every $t$ and satisfies $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

**(iv) Time-dependent families.** A prescribed time-dependent family $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators is a different model assumption: a norm-continuous finite-dimensional Hermitian family is used only through the unitary two-time propagator that its family defines, and the exponential of the integral of $H(t)$ is not identified with that propagator unless the family commutes with itself at different times. The general unbounded time-dependent case requires a separate existence and domain theorem of its own and is not adopted by this postulate; the driven-dynamics page states its own assumptions for the models it treats.

**(v) Open systems.** A non-unitary evolution of the reduced description of a system coupled to an environment is an extension obtained from an explicitly chosen environment model and a declared reduction, not a replacement for clause (ii); no environment model is adopted by this postulate.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the isolated-system idealization. They assert nothing about the origin of the energy operator of a concrete system, about the accuracy of the idealization for a laboratory preparation, or about which laboratory interactions realize an isolated evolution; those are tested identifications in the sense of P7.
premise_quotes: [F1] [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]: the declared closed-system state evolves by $\rho(t)=U_t\rho_0U_t^*$ with $U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ and unitary group law.

Assume AC and Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a self-adjoint quantum Hamiltonian bounded below with a complete discrete energy eigenfamily of finite multiplicity, and let $\rho_0$ be any positive trace-class density operator of trace one. Let $\hbar>0$ be the assigned action constant in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, adopt the unitary dynamics $U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ of [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], and assume the trace-class Gibbs and local moment conditions of [[pthm-td-general-quantum-canonical-identities]] that supply this discrete eigenfamily. Then, conditional on the current batch-12 draft theorem [[thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-dephasing]], the Cesaro state
$$\bar\rho_\tau:=\frac1{\tau}\int_0^\tau U_t\rho_0U_t^*\,dt$$
converges in trace norm as $\tau\to\infty$ to $\rho_{\mathrm{diag}}=\sum_E P_E\rho_0P_E$, where $P_E$ is the spectral projection onto the full eigenspace of energy $E$. Coherences inside degenerate energy blocks remain. The limit need not be Gibbs, and no pointwise-in-time convergence or thermalization is asserted.

review.evidence: Self-adjoint spectral calculus gives unit-modulus exponential, unitary group and strong continuity; conjugation preserves positivity and trace. Two-site consumer has a finite diagonal H and ground eigenvector, so its phase is exactly one and its density remains fixed. Both explicitly assume AC and Countable Choice and fix hbar>0 and the dimensionless energy-time phase.

Adopt the canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] together with the
state, probability, dynamics and preparation postulates P1, P2, P4, P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-dimensional sector class of the entropy definition: the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] has sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ of finite dimension $D\ge1$ with self-adjoint energy
operator $H_N^\sigma$, assigned temperature $T>0$, inverse temperature
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ and eigen-decomposition
$H_N^\sigma=\sum_{j=1}^DE_jT_{v_j,v_j}$ with orthonormal eigenbasis
$(v_1,\dots,v_D)$ and real eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_D$. Write
$q_j:=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N$ with $Z_N:=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$,
$\rho_\beta:=\sum_jq_jT_{v_j,v_j}$, and let
$F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho)$ and
$F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-k_BT\log Z_N$ be the free-energy functional and
equilibrium free energy of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] clauses (e).
Then:

(a) *the canonical preparation*: $Z_N\in(0,\infty)$ is a finite sum,
$q_j>0$, $\sum_jq_j=1$, and $\rho_\beta$ is a declared sector preparation of
the model with
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)=\frac1{Z_N}\sum_{j=1}^DE_je^{-\beta E_j},\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z_N+\beta\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma);$$

(b) *free-energy minimum*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ one
has $F(\rho)\ge F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_BT\log Z_N$;

(c) *uniqueness*: equality $F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$ holds if and only if
$\rho=\rho_\beta$; consequently the canonical preparation is the unique
minimiser of the free-energy functional over the declared sector
preparations, and $F(\rho_\beta)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$;

(d) *degenerate case*: if $H_N^\sigma=c\,\mathrm{id}$ for a real $c$, then
$Z_N=De^{-\beta c}$, $\rho_\beta=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$,
$s(\rho_\beta)=\log D$ and $F_{\mathrm{eq}}=c-k_BT\log D$;

(e) *scope*: the statement is conditional on the adopted ensemble postulate
and on the declared finite-dimensional model; it asserts no equilibration of
any preparation towards $\rho_\beta$, no rate of approach, no thermodynamic
limit, no pressure or volume variable, and, for a laboratory sample, it
inherits the tested identification of the preparation and temperature
assignment of P7.

Their current statements and the theorem proof were inspected, but their published records lack the required audit/source-review evidence, so this use remains escalated.

Work in the nonzero finite-dimensional fixed-$N$ sector of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], with self-adjoint energy $H_N^\sigma$ in joules and assigned $T>0$ in kelvins. Adopt the Gibbs preparation of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] and its unit convention $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$. For $F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-T S(\rho)$ over the declared sector density operators, the canonical preparation is the unique minimizer and
$$\min_\rho F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log\operatorname{tr}(e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}).$$
This quantum statistical functional is not identified here with a macroscopic Helmholtz potential without an additional model bridge; its minimum does not establish equilibration.

review.evidence: Independently checked the scalar log tangent inequality including zero weights. In the two orthonormal eigenbases, p_ij is doubly stochastic and r_i=sum_j p_ij q_j>0. The TD consumer has precisely the nonzero finite fixed-sector, assigned T>0, entropy functional, adopted preparation and stated Choice assumptions. No infinite sector or dynamical minimizer claim is used.

[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for the mode models
declared below, the state and probability postulates P1, P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],

Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Temperatures are assigned as in
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], so that
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$. Declare the occupation readouts as assigned sharp observables $(N,1)$ and $(N_-,1)$, with unit particle-count, which is dimensionless. The total particle-number operator $\mathcal N$ in the countable-mode reading has the same unit; every occupation mean and higher number moment below is read in the corresponding dimensionless count unit. Then:

(a) *single bosonic mode*: let $F(\mathbb C)$ be the one-mode Fock space with
number operator $N$ and orthonormal number basis $(e_n)$
([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]]), let
$\varepsilon>0$ and let the model declare the energy operator $H:=\varepsilon N$
on $F(\mathbb C)$; the model's canonical preparation at temperature $T$ is
$\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z$ with $Z=(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$, the
number readout $N$ is an assigned sharp observable with finite thermal mean
$$\langle N\rangle_\beta=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}=\frac1{e^{\varepsilon/(k_BT)}-1},$$
and all moments $\langle N^k\rangle_\beta$, $k\ge1$, are finite;

(b) *single fermionic orbital and grand-canonical shift*: on
$\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^2$ with occupation operator $N_-$ and

the same formula is the model's thermal mean when $\mu=0$ and
$\varepsilon_1>0$;

(c) *countably many independent modes*: let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$
and $\mu\in\mathbb R$, and let the model declare the free-mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ (one mode case of clause (a)) with the product reading of
